chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, [from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him)], said:
I asked him about a man who made it upon himself to walk to the House of Allah, and he could not do it. He said: 'He should perform Hajj riding.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who vowed to walk to Mecca for Hajj but cannot?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on Vows, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *kaffarah* (expiation) or flexible fulfillment for unfulfillable vows, prioritizing the intent over rigid literalism. It reflects the Shia juristic view that physical incapacity excuses the specific mode of worship, allowing the rider to fulfill the obligation without penalty, thereby preventing undue hardship (*haraj*).
